summary:
COSMORA is a 3D space mission game where you build a spacecraft, launch it, travel to another world, land, and explore with a rover.

You start in the Vehicle Assembly Bay, where you can customize your rocket’s colors, boosters, fairing, lander insulation, and engine plume. Then a crawler carries the rocket to the launchpad. During ascent, you control the rocket, watch flight information, and separate stages as needed. After reaching Earth orbit, you wait for the right moment and fire the transfer burn to travel toward your chosen destination.

Each world has its own gravity, terrain, and science targets. During landing, you steer toward the safe zone and manage your descent speed. A hard landing or entering a hazard area destroys the lander. Once safely on the surface, you drive a six-wheeled rover, scan science targets, avoid rocks, and search for hidden rare samples.

Completing missions and scanning targets earns credits. Rare samples also unlock special spacecraft parts. Your credits and unlocked items are saved in the browser, so they remain available when you return.

COSMORA uses React, TypeScript, Three.js, and Tailwind CSS. Its environments, spacecraft, terrain, visual effects, and sounds are generated by code, creating a playable simulator without requiring large collections of external assets.
details:
What does COSMORA do, and how does it work?

COSMORA is a 3D space mission simulator. Players customize a rocket, launch it, reach Earth orbit, perform a transfer burn, land on a selected planet, and explore with a rover. The game guides players through each mission phase with controls, telemetry, warnings, landing zones, and science targets. It also includes credits and unlockable parts that save in the browser.

What benefits does it have?

COSMORA makes space exploration concepts interactive. Players can learn about rocket staging, orbital transfers, planetary gravity, spacecraft control, and landing challenges by trying them in a simulated mission. It also encourages problem-solving, planning, and curiosity about planets and space technology.

What is the intended impact of the project?

The project aims to make space science more engaging and approachable, especially for students and people interested in space or game development. It turns mission ideas into a playable experience that can spark interest in real space missions and engineering.

What tools, languages, hardware, and software were used?

The project uses React 19 and TypeScript for the interface and game logic, Three.js for 3D graphics, Tailwind CSS v4 for styling, and Vite for development and building. It also uses browser technologies such as WebGL, Canvas, Web Audio, and localStorage. Development requires a computer capable of running a modern browser; players need a browser that supports WebGL.

How is the project creative?

COSMORA combines rocket construction, orbital flight, planetary landing, rover driving, and a credits system in one experience. It uses procedural code to create spacecraft, terrain, textures, effects, and sounds. Players can customize their vehicles, explore different worlds, and hunt for rare samples that unlock special parts.

What factors did the team consider?

The team considered realistic-feeling mission stages, clear controls, readable flight information, different planetary conditions, safe and hazardous landing areas, rover collisions, and progression rewards. They also considered performance on ordinary computers and designed the game to run in a web browser without requiring large external asset files.
